exports.name: AutoWarp
exports.summary: How a file plays in time at an arrangement's tempo, as `autoWarp` works it out.

exports.name: autoWarp
exports.summary: The warp that plays a recording of `duration` seconds in time at `tempo` BPM (CLP-019): a short one that a whole number of 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 bars fits at its estimated tempo, as that loop, marked at its start and end; any other on a marker at the first beat of each bar, moved onto the transient within an eighth of a beat.

exports.name: detectTransients
exports.summary: Where `channels` have their transients, in seconds: each frame where the level rises sharply above what it does around it, found to the sample where the slope first reaches half its height there.

exports.name: TempoEstimate
exports.summary: A recording's tempo, as `@audio/beat-detect` reads it and the registry's `analyzeBeat` fits it to the transients.

exports.name: CompressorSettings
exports.summary: The transfer curve of a compressor: the output level in dB for each input level in dB, the textbook curve with a knee centred on the threshold, what a plug-in draws.

exports.name: compressorOutput
exports.summary: A compressor's transfer curve: the output level in dB for each input level in dB.

exports.name: BiquadSettings
exports.summary: One filter as `biquadResponse` draws it: its type, frequency, gain and Q, at a sample rate.

exports.name: BiquadType
exports.summary: The kinds of band an equalizer draws: cuts, shelves, a peak, a notch and a band-pass.

exports.name: bandGainForHandle
exports.summary: The inverse, for dragging: the gain a band needs at `frequency` for its handle to sit at `responseDb` on the curve, so the handle follows the pointer one to one instead of the gain drifting from it.

exports.name: bandHandleDb
exports.summary: Where a band's handle sits on an equalizer's curve: the response of all the bands at the band's own frequency.

exports.name: biquadResponse
exports.summary: A biquad's gain in dB at `hz`, 0 being unity.

exports.name: EqBand
exports.summary: One band of an equalizer: a filter that can be switched out of the chain.

exports.name: eqResponse
exports.summary: An equalizer's bands in series: their gains in dB add up at each frequency.

exports.name: SAMPLE_RATE
exports.summary: The sample rate a curve is drawn at unless a band says another.

exports.name: toWebAudioQ
exports.summary: The value to give a `BiquadFilterNode`'s `Q` for a band's `q`.

exports.name: WEB_AUDIO_FILTER_TYPES
exports.summary: The Web Audio `BiquadFilterNode` type that does what each band type draws.

exports.name: dbToGain
exports.summary: The amplitude ratio of a level in dB: 0 dB is 1, -6.02 dB is 0.5.

exports.name: gainToDb
exports.summary: The level in dB of an amplitude ratio: 1 is 0 dB, 0.5 is -6.02 dB.

exports.name: peakDb
exports.summary: The level in dBFS of the loudest sample of `samples`, either way: how near the signal comes to clipping, where `rmsDb` says how loud it sounds.

exports.name: rmsDb
exports.summary: The RMS level of `samples` in dBFS: 0 dB for a square wave at full scale, -3 dB for a sine at full scale.

exports.name: createLoudnessMeter
exports.summary: Measures what is connected to it while it plays, on the audio thread, and calls `onLoudness` with its momentary, short-term and integrated loudness every 100 ms.

exports.name: createLoudnessReader
exports.summary: Reads loudness block by block: `add` takes the K-weighted mean square of the next 100 ms, summed over the channels, as the meter's processor posts it, and gives the loudness up to it.

exports.name: LiveLoudness
exports.summary: How loud a sound is while it plays, in LUFS.

exports.name: LOUDNESS_TARGETS
exports.summary: Targets in LUFS: what streaming services, podcasts and broadcast (EBU R 128) ask a file to be.

exports.name: LOUDNESS_WORKLET
exports.summary: The meter's processor: it K-weights each channel of its input (a high shelf, then a high-pass, with the coefficients `@audio/weighting-k` gives for the context's rate), and posts the mean square of each block of 100 ms, summed over the channels.

exports.name: Loudness
exports.summary: How loud a sound is.

exports.name: LoudnessMeter
exports.summary: A live loudness meter on a context, as `createLoudnessMeter` makes it.

exports.name: loudnessGain
exports.summary: The gain in dB that brings a sound to `target` LUFS, as far as its true peak stays at or under `ceiling` dBTP: a sound that would pass it lands under the target instead, and nothing is limited.

exports.name: measureLoudness
exports.summary: Measures whole channels at once.

exports.name: AudioPeaks
exports.summary: The lowest and highest sample of each slice of the audio, -1 to 1: what the Waveform draws as the waveform really is, lopsided where the audio is.

exports.name: computePeaks
exports.summary: Reduces PCM samples to `bucketCount` slices, keeping each slice's lowest and highest sample across every channel, a take panned hard to one side still draws, rather than reading as a flat line on the channel it isn't on.

exports.name: downsampleWaveform
exports.summary: Downsamples raw PCM samples into `targetLength` blocks, each block's value the peak (max) absolute amplitude within it, the reduction waveform visualizers use, since a block average flattens short transients into a softer-looking curve than the audio actually has.

exports.name: normalizePeaks
exports.summary: Scales peaks so the loudest sample, either way, reaches full height, keeping each slice's lopsidedness.

exports.name: normalizeWaveform
exports.summary: Scales `values` so the largest entry becomes 1, keeps a waveform's peak reaching full height regardless of the source audio's own loudness.

exports.name: SpectrumBandsOptions
exports.summary: The frequencies and levels `spectrumBands` spreads its bands over.

exports.name: spectrumBands
exports.summary: Reduces an analyser's spectrum (`getFloatFrequencyData`: decibels per frequency bin) to `bands.length` levels of 0-1, low to high, written into `bands`.

exports.name: DetectPitchOptions
exports.summary: What `detectPitch` looks for.

exports.name: detectPitch
exports.summary: The pitch the samples hold and how clear it is, or nothing: too quiet a signal, or no clear period.

exports.name: PitchEstimate
exports.summary: What a detection found: the pitch and how periodic the sound is there.

exports.name: analyzeBeat
exports.summary: Reads a recording's beat, once, as it is decoded: what `warpOnImport` warps its clips by.

exports.name: audioChroma
exports.summary: How much of a recording's sound lies in each pitch class, C to B, summing to 1, read once as it is decoded: what a key is read from, with notes or without (`detectKeys` of the Scale menu).

exports.name: BeatAnalysis
exports.summary: What a recording's beat is read as when it comes in: its tempo, if it has one, and its transients, in seconds.

exports.name: ACX
exports.summary: What ACX asks of an audiobook: the RMS between -23 and -18 dBFS, the peak at most -3 dBFS, the noise floor at most -60 dBFS RMS.

exports.name: AcxCheck
exports.summary: One requirement and how the sound stands against it.

exports.name: AcxReport
exports.summary: A sound against the ACX audiobook requirements.

exports.name: checkAcx
exports.summary: Checks a sound against ACX's requirements for an audiobook.

exports.name: reportSound
exports.summary: Reads a sound once, to tell what it is: its loudness, its key, its tempo, and whether it meets ACX's requirements.

exports.name: SoundReport
exports.summary: What `reportSound` reads from a sound.

exports.name: detectSilences
exports.summary: Where `channels` pause between their sounds, as `[from, to]` in seconds, in order: each stretch of at least `minDuration` where every sample of every channel stays under the threshold, found to a block of 1024 frames.

exports.name: SilenceOptions
exports.summary: What `detectSilences` takes, both optional.

exports.name: SPECTRA_SIZE
exports.summary: The frames of a window of the spectra, and of one of their columns: 2048, some 43 ms at 48 kHz, the window a spectrogram fits a view with.

exports.name: Spectra
exports.summary: A recording summed up as spectra, for a spectrogram drawn on the GPU that does not hold the recording: a column every `hop` frames, each bin's level from DC to Nyquist over windows of `size` frames, a byte each.

exports.name: SpectraSource
exports.summary: A reader of a recording, mixed to one: how many frames it holds, and its frames from `from` to `to`, at once or later.

exports.name: spectrogramSpectra
exports.summary: The spectra of a recording (`Spectra`): a column every `hop` frames, each bin's power over the Hann windows of `size` frames centred in the column every `size / 2` frames (the short-time transform of `@audio/stft`), their mean, as a byte.

exports.name: holdPeaks
exports.summary: Keeps the loudest level each point of a spectrum reached: a peak rises with the spectrum at once, stays put for `hold` seconds, then falls at `fall` dB per second until the spectrum meets it again.

exports.name: LogSpectrumOptions
exports.summary: The frequencies the axis of `logSpectrum` spans.

exports.name: logSpectrum
exports.summary: Fills `out` with `bins` (dB per analyser bin, as `getFloatFrequencyData` writes them) resampled onto a log axis.

exports.name: PeakHoldOptions
exports.summary: How long `holdPeaks` holds a peak, and how fast it lets it fall.

exports.name: SPECTRUM_FLOOR_DB
exports.summary: The quietest a point is drawn: what a silent bin, `-Infinity` dB, becomes.

exports.name: stereoCorrelation
exports.summary: How alike the two channels of a sound are, from -1 to 1, as a correlation meter reads it: 1 when both carry the same sound (mono, at any levels), 0 when they have nothing in common or only one side sounds, and -1 when one is the other upside down, which cancels out once the two are summed to mono.

exports.name: BandShares
exports.summary: What each slice of a sound is made of: the share of its lows, mids and highs, the loudest of the three being 1.

exports.name: Bands
exports.summary: The three bands of a stretch of sound: its lows under 250 Hz, its highs over 2.5 kHz, and the mids between.

exports.name: bandShares
exports.summary: Reads a sound as `count` slices of equal length, each by how its energy is spread over three bands: the lows under 250 Hz, the highs over 2.5 kHz and the mids between.

exports.name: createBandSplit
exports.summary: Splits a sound in three a stretch at a time, as `splitBands` does: each call takes the stretch that follows the one before and carries the crossover's state over, so stretches split in order are the sound split whole.

exports.name: SplitBands
exports.summary: A sound as three signals: what it has under 250 Hz, between, and over 2.5 kHz.

exports.name: splitBands
exports.summary: The sound's channels mixed to one and split in three by a Linkwitz-Riley crossover (`@audio/eq-crossover`, 24 dB an octave) at 250 Hz and 2.5 kHz: the three bands add back to the mix, level and phase.

exports.name: ChoiceOption
exports.summary: One entry of a choice: the `value` that goes in the state and the `label` a panel shows.

exports.name: ChoiceParameter
exports.summary: A pick from a short list: a waveform, a filter type, a mode.

exports.name: Device
exports.summary: A defined device: its parameters, and everything that reads or changes a state of it, with no sound and no view.

exports.name: DeviceApplied
exports.summary: What `apply` returns: the new state, the changes made, and the changes refused with their reason.

exports.name: DeviceBinding
exports.summary: What a host gives a device to drive: an engine, a view, a store.

exports.name: DeviceChange
exports.summary: One parameter `apply` changed.

exports.name: DeviceContext
exports.summary: What the host knows and the device does not: the tempo a time parameter that follows it is read against.

exports.name: DeviceDefinition
exports.summary: What `defineDevice` takes: the device's id, name, description and parameters, and whether it is an instrument, takes a sidechain or adds latency.

exports.name: DeviceDefinitionError
exports.summary: Raised when a device is defined with parameters that cannot work.

exports.name: DeviceDescription
exports.summary: A device as an agent or a catalog reads it.

exports.name: DeviceReadings
exports.summary: What a device reports about what it is doing right now, for a meter.

exports.name: DeviceRejection
exports.summary: One parameter `apply` did not change, and why.

exports.name: DeviceSignalName
exports.summary: What a device's engine lets a host watch of its sound beyond its input and its output.

exports.name: DeviceState
exports.summary: The state of a device: each parameter's id to its value.

exports.name: defineDevice
exports.summary: Defines a device from its parameters.

exports.name: NumberParameter
exports.summary: A continuous parameter: a number in a range, on a scale, in steps.

exports.name: ParameterDescription
exports.summary: A parameter as an agent or a catalog reads it: JSON-safe, with no function in it.

exports.name: ParameterDescriptor
exports.summary: A parameter of a device: a number, a toggle or a choice.

exports.name: ParameterValue
exports.summary: What a parameter holds: a number, a boolean or the value of a choice.

exports.name: ToggleParameter
exports.summary: An on or off parameter: a bypass, a mode, an auto switch.

exports.name: createFeed
exports.summary: Feeds a worklet only while the path it plays is heard: a worklet fed nothing costs nothing.

exports.name: createWorkletStage
exports.summary: A stage of an engine that runs a worklet: the sound passes clean while the worklet loads, then fades over to it.

exports.name: DeviceTaps
exports.summary: The points of an engine's graph a host may listen to beyond its input and its output, by the names its device declares in `signals`.

exports.name: EffectEngine
exports.summary: The engine of an effect on the Web Audio API: the binding of its state (`update`, `dispose`, `readings`) between an input and an output.

exports.name: EngineFactory
exports.summary: What every `create<Name>Engine` is: an engine on a context, for the state it starts with and the host's tempo.

exports.name: FEED_RELEASE_MS
exports.summary: How long after a path stops a worklet is still fed, in ms: its fade is over by then.

exports.name: Feed
exports.summary: Connections made while a path plays and taken away once it has faded out.

exports.name: FeedConnection
exports.summary: A connection a feed makes: `from` into `to`, at an output and an input of their own if given.

exports.name: InstrumentEngine
exports.summary: The engine of an instrument: one voice, notes in, sound out.

exports.name: NoiseColor
exports.summary: The colors of noise a buffer is made in, as `@audio/synth-noise` makes them.

exports.name: noiseBuffer
exports.summary: Two seconds of noise on a context, from `@audio/synth-noise` (seeded, its peak at 0.9), made once per color and context and shared by everything that plays it: a synth's noise source, a snare's rattle, the pink noise an equalizer is heard through.

exports.name: WorkletStage
exports.summary: A worklet that takes over from the clean sound once it is in the graph.

exports.name: InstrumentBinding
exports.summary: What a host gives an instrument to play: a `DeviceBinding` that also takes notes.

exports.name: NoteTiming
exports.summary: When a note starts or ends, and which note it is.

exports.name: playNote
exports.summary: Plays a note for `seconds` on an instrument: `noteOn` now, `noteOff` when the time is up.

exports.name: SidechainBinding
exports.summary: What a host gives a device that takes a key signal: a `DeviceBinding` whose engine has a second input, `sidechain`, that the key is connected to.

exports.name: measureLatency
exports.summary: How long an engine delays a signal, in milliseconds: where what comes out of an impulse lines up with it.

exports.name: measureResponse
exports.summary: How far an engine's frequency response is from `curve`, the gain in dB the device draws at each frequency.

exports.name: ResponseMeasurement
exports.summary: What a measurement of a frequency response found.

exports.name: LINEAR_SCALE
exports.summary: Even steps: the right feel for levels, times and anything heard in differences.

exports.name: LOGARITHMIC_SCALE
exports.summary: Even ratios: the right feel for frequency, Q, ratios and times heard in proportions.

exports.name: ParameterScale
exports.summary: How a value maps onto a control's travel, and back.

exports.name: ParameterScaleProp
exports.summary: A scale as a parameter takes it: `"linear"`, `"log"`, or a scale of your own.

exports.name: resolveScale
exports.summary: The scale a parameter names: `"linear"` and `"log"` as the two above, a scale of your own as it is.

exports.name: DeviceTool
exports.summary: A tool a model can call to drive a device: agent-agnostic, with no SDK in it.

exports.name: DeviceToolResult
exports.summary: What a tool's `run` returns: the state after the call, a summary for the model, and the note to play for a `<id>_play` call.

exports.name: deviceTools
exports.summary: The tools that drive a device, derived from its parameters: `<id>_set` takes any of its parameters by id, `<id>_reset` puts some or all back to their defaults.

exports.name: JsonSchema
exports.summary: The subset of JSON Schema the tools use: what OpenAI, Anthropic, MCP and the AI SDK all accept as an input schema.

exports.name: NOTE_DURATION
exports.summary: How long a note lasts when a call does not say, and the shortest and longest it may ask for, in seconds.

exports.name: highshelf
exports.summary: High-shelf.

exports.name: lowshelf
exports.summary: Low-shelf.

exports.name: magnitude
exports.summary: |H(f)| of one section at frequency `f` — analysis/plotting.

exports.name: compandStream
exports.summary: { write, flush } streaming primitive underlying the default export's streaming form.

exports.name: compressorGain
exports.summary: Soft-knee downward compression curve.

exports.name: compressor
exports.summary: The smooth compressor's manifest: an AudioWorklet processor's parameters and state, as its package publishes them.

exports.name: deesser
exports.summary: The de-esser's manifest: its processor's parameters and latency.

exports.name: expanderGain
exports.summary: Soft-knee downward expansion curve.

exports.name: upwardExpanderGain
exports.summary: Soft-knee upward expansion curve — the above-threshold complement of expanderGain.

exports.name: expander
exports.summary: The expander's manifest: its processor's parameters and modes.

exports.name: fet
exports.summary: The FET compressor model's manifest.

exports.name: limiterLatency
exports.summary: Samples the output trails the input by: the lookahead, and 96 with `truePeak`.

exports.name: opto
exports.summary: The opto compressor model's manifest.

exports.name: unlimitDeficitGain
exports.summary: adaptive (default) pure mapping: transient deficit (crestTarget − peak-held transientness) → target lift (dB), gated by onset presence.

exports.name: unlimitGain
exports.summary: adaptive:false pure mapping: transientness (fast-over-slow envelope gap, dB) → target lift (dB), before ballistic smoothing.

exports.name: unlimit
exports.summary: The de-limiter's manifest: its processor's parameters.

exports.name: varimu
exports.summary: The vari-mu compressor model's manifest.

exports.name: vca
exports.summary: The VCA compressor model's manifest.

exports.name: distortion
exports.summary: Mutates `data` in place and returns the same reference.

exports.name: diodeLadder
exports.summary: The diode ladder filter, run over a buffer in place.

exports.name: korg35
exports.summary: The Korg35 filter, run over a buffer in place.

exports.name: moogLadder
exports.summary: The Moog ladder filter, two or four poles, run over a buffer in place.

exports.name: oberheim
exports.summary: The Oberheim SEM state-variable filter, run over a buffer in place.

exports.name: dattorro
exports.summary: Process in place.

exports.name: fdn
exports.summary: Process in place.

exports.name: freeverb
exports.summary: Process in place.

exports.name: schroeder
exports.summary: Process a mono buffer in place; returns the same array.

exports.name: spring
exports.summary: Process a mono buffer in place; returns the same array.

exports.name: decodeAudioChannels
exports.summary: Decodes raw audio bytes, such as `file.arrayBuffer()`, into every channel's PCM samples at the context's sample rate, ready for `computePeaks`.

exports.name: decodeAudioSamples
exports.summary: Decodes raw audio bytes into one channel's PCM samples, ready for `downsampleWaveform`: `decodeAudioChannels`, then the channel asked for, or the last there is.

exports.name: AudioFileFormat
exports.summary: The formats `encodeAudio` writes.

exports.name: downloadFile
exports.summary: Saves a file through the browser's downloads, named `name`.

exports.name: EncodeAudioOptions
exports.summary: What `encodeAudio` writes: the format, its bit depth or bitrate, the channels' sample rate, and a callback for its progress.

exports.name: encodeAudio
exports.summary: Encodes channels of samples, from -1 to 1, as a file.

exports.name: CHANNEL_LAYOUTS
exports.summary: The layouts a sound can be mixed to: one channel, two, or the surround layouts of film.

exports.name: LAYOUT_CHANNELS
exports.summary: How many channels a layout has.

exports.name: mixChannels
exports.summary: The same sound in another layout: a down-mix folds the centre and the surrounds into the sides at -3 dB and drops the low-frequency channel, and scales so the sum stays at full scale at most; an up-mix keeps the sides where they are, spreads them to the surrounds at -6 dB and leaves the centre and the low-frequency channel silent.

exports.name: padChannels
exports.summary: Silence, in samples, added before and after the sound.

exports.name: repeatChannels
exports.summary: The sound played `times` times in a row, the first included.

exports.name: resampleChannels
exports.summary: Every channel at another sample rate, by a windowed sinc: the same sound, heard as a converter of that rate would give it, over `channels.length` arrays as long as the new rate needs.

exports.name: reverseChannels
exports.summary: Every channel played backwards: the end first.

exports.name: downloadMidiFile
exports.summary: Saves the notes as a `.mid` file, named `filename`.

exports.name: MIDI_FILE_ACCEPT
exports.summary: What a file input or a drop zone accepts as a MIDI file.

exports.name: MidiFileGrid
exports.summary: The grid notes are read onto: steps a quarter note, the clip's length in steps, and the pitch and tempo ranges it takes.

exports.name: readMidiFile
exports.summary: Reads a MIDI file's notes onto a grid of steps, with the file's own tempo (clamped to the BPM range).

exports.name: readMidiFileParts
exports.summary: Reads a MIDI file as parts, for a host that lays each on a track of its own: a part per track and channel, named after its track (and its channel, when a track holds several), its notes in beats as they were written, not quantized and not cut, at least a tick long, and the first program its channel plays.

exports.name: ScoreNote
exports.summary: A note of a score in beats: where it starts and how long it lasts, in quarter notes.

exports.name: ScorePart
exports.summary: One part of a score: its name, whether it is drums, and its notes in beats.

exports.name: writeMidiFile
exports.summary: The notes as a Standard MIDI File, the inverse of `readMidiFile`.

exports.name: downloadMusicXmlFile
exports.summary: Saves the notes as a `.musicxml` file, named `filename`.

exports.name: MUSICXML_FILE_ACCEPT
exports.summary: What a file input or a drop zone accepts as a MusicXML file: a score, or one compressed as `.mxl`.

exports.name: MusicXmlFileGrid
exports.summary: The grid notes are read onto: steps a quarter note, the clip's length in steps, and the pitch and tempo ranges it takes.

exports.name: readMusicXmlFile
exports.summary: Reads a MusicXML score's notes onto a grid of steps, with its first tempo (clamped to the BPM range), every part into the one clip.

exports.name: readMusicXmlFileParts
exports.summary: Reads a MusicXML score as parts, for a host that lays each on a track of its own: a part each, by its name, its notes in beats as they were written, through changes of tempo, not quantized and not cut.

exports.name: writeMusicXmlFile
exports.summary: The notes as a MusicXML score, the inverse of `readMusicXmlFile`, for a notation app to open: on the grid they sit on, so nothing moves.

exports.name: DITHER_METHODS
exports.summary: How a sound is brought to fewer bits: `tpdf` adds triangular noise one step wide before rounding, so the error is steady noise instead of distortion that follows the sound; `shaped` does the same with the error fed back through two delays, which moves the noise up toward the highest frequencies, where the ear hears it least; `feedback` rounds with the error fed back once (`@audio/effect-noiseshaper`), with no added noise.

exports.name: ditherChannels
exports.summary: Every channel rounded to `bits` bits, by one of `DITHER_METHODS`, the way a sound is mastered to 16 bits or 8: as many steps as that depth has, and the error made into noise by the method.

exports.name: FilterType
exports.summary: A filter's shape: what it lets through, 12 dB an octave.

exports.name: filterChannels
exports.summary: Every channel through one filter of the cookbook, at `frequency` in hertz and a `q` (one over the square root of two by default, the flattest).

exports.name: gainChannels
exports.summary: Every channel, `db` louder or quieter.

exports.name: NormalizeTarget
exports.summary: What a sound is normalized to: its loudest sample, or its integrated loudness held under a true-peak ceiling.

exports.name: normalizeChannels
exports.summary: The sound, with one gain on every channel, so the balance between them stays: to a peak in dBFS, or to a loudness in LUFS as far as its true peak stays under `ceiling` (-1 dBTP by default).

exports.name: panChannels
exports.summary: A sound's balance: -1 is all left, 1 all right, 0 as it is.

exports.name: SHIFT_METHODS
exports.summary: How a pitch is shifted: let the library choose from the sound (`auto`), or a method by name.

exports.name: STRETCH_METHODS
exports.summary: The ways a sound is stretched in time with its pitch kept, each with what it suits: a phase vocoder that keeps the attacks of drums (`transient`), one for general music (`pvocLock`), waveform overlap-add for speech made shorter (`wsola`) or longer (`pvsola`), a vocoder with the harmonic and percussive parts apart for full mixes (`hybrid`), and the extreme stretch of ambient textures (`paulstretch`).

exports.name: shiftChannels
exports.summary: Every channel `semitones` higher or lower, its length unchanged.

exports.name: speedChannels
exports.summary: The sound played `speed` times as fast, its pitch moving with it as on a tape or a record: 2 is twice as fast and an octave up.

exports.name: stretchChannels
exports.summary: Every channel `factor` times as long, its pitch unchanged: 2 is twice as slow, 0.5 twice as fast.

exports.name: FormatOptions
exports.summary: What every formatter takes, over its own defaults.

exports.name: LevelUnit
exports.summary: The units of a level: decibels of a gain, of full scale, of a true peak, of a voltage; loudness in LUFS and its range in LU.

exports.name: formatLevel
exports.summary: A level or a gain: `-6.0 dBFS`, `-23.0 LUFS`, `+3.0 dB`, `-1.0 dBTP`.

exports.name: FrequencyStyle
exports.summary: How a frequency is written: by size (`auto`), always in hertz, or always in kilohertz.

exports.name: formatFrequency
exports.summary: A frequency: `120 Hz`, `1.2 kHz`, `12 kHz`.

exports.name: formatSampleRate
exports.summary: A sample rate: `44.1 kHz`, `48 kHz`, `11.025 kHz`: in kilohertz, with the places it needs and no more.

exports.name: TimeStyle
exports.summary: How a time is written: a clock to the second, a clock to the millisecond, or a length in seconds.

exports.name: formatTime
exports.summary: A time: `1:05` (`clock`), `1:05.250` (`precise`, to the millisecond, with hours past an hour: `1:02:03.500`), or `65.25 s` (`seconds`).

exports.name: formatDuration
exports.summary: A length of time by its size: `120 ms` under a second, `1.25 s` above.

exports.name: formatTempo
exports.summary: The tempo, `120 BPM`, with a decimal only when it has one.

exports.name: NoteOptions
exports.summary: How a note is spelled: sharps or flats, the octave of the middle C (`4` in scientific pitch, `3` on Yamaha's), and the typographic ♯ and ♭ or plain `#` and `b`.

exports.name: formatNote
exports.summary: A MIDI note as a name: `60` is `C4`, `61` `C#4`, `69` `A4`.

exports.name: PanStyle
exports.summary: How a pan is written: `L30`, `C`, `R30` (`lr`), or a signed number, `-30`, `0`, `+30` (`signed`).

exports.name: formatPan

exports.summary: `adaptive` follows the zoom; a fixed division stays put however far you zoom.

exports.name: GridIntervalOptions
exports.summary: How close adaptive grid lines may be, and whether the grid is in triplets.

exports.name: gridInterval
exports.summary: Seconds between grid lines at `zoom` px per second: the lines a timeline draws and the step it snaps to, so what you see is where you land.

exports.name: gridLabel
exports.summary: Names an interval the way a grid readout does: "1 bar", "4 bars", "1/16", "1/8T".

exports.name: METRONOME_RHYTHMS
exports.summary: How often a metronome clicks: with the beat, or a note value, straight or triplet.

exports.name: MetronomeRhythm
exports.summary: The id of a metronome rhythm: `"auto"` (the beat), a bar, or a note value, straight or triplet.

exports.name: metronomeRhythmSeconds
exports.summary: Seconds between clicks for a rhythm, or `null` for `auto`, which has no interval of its own: it is the beat, whatever the signature makes one.

exports.name: SYNCED_DIVISIONS
exports.summary: The note values a time parameter that follows the tempo can take, shortest first: `1/16` is a sixteenth note, `1/8t` a triplet eighth (two thirds of it) and `1/8d` a dotted eighth (one and a half times it).

exports.name: SyncedDivision
exports.summary: A note value as `syncedSeconds` reads it: `"1/8"`, its triplet `"1/8t"` or its dotted `"1/8d"`.

exports.name: syncedSeconds
exports.summary: How long a synced note value lasts at `tempo`, in seconds: `1/8` an eighth, `1/8t` its triplet, `1/8d` its dotted one.

exports.name: TRIPLET_FACTOR
exports.summary: Three in the space of two: a triplet division is 2/3 of its straight one.

exports.name: Bar
exports.summary: A bar as a ruler draws it.

exports.name: barsBeatsWith
exports.summary: Where `seconds` falls in bars, beats and sixteenths through the signature changes, each counted from one.

exports.name: barsOf
exports.summary: The bars from 0 to `until` seconds, through the signature changes: whole bars of each signature, and a partial bar where a change cuts one short.

exports.name: isSignature
exports.summary: Whether a signature is one a bar can have: 1 to 99 beats of a whole, half, quarter, eighth or sixteenth note.

exports.name: MetronomeClick
exports.summary: A click of a metronome.

exports.name: metronomeClicks
exports.summary: The clicks of a metronome from 0 to `until` seconds, through the signature changes.

exports.name: SignatureChange
exports.summary: A new signature from `at` on, in seconds: `beatsPerBar` beats of a `beatUnit` note.

exports.name: advance
exports.summary: Advances `cursor`, emitting every step boundary now within `SCHEDULE_AHEAD_SECONDS` of `now`.

exports.name: anchoredCursor
exports.summary: A cursor that emits `step` at `now`, the seed for `start()` and for every re-anchor (seek, region commit).

exports.name: anchorForTempoChange
exports.summary: The anchor to carry on with when the tempo changes while playing.

exports.name: MAX_CATCH_UP_SECONDS
exports.summary: How late a boundary may be and still be played, half a second.

exports.name: positionAt
exports.summary: The continuous playhead position, in fractional full-grid steps, at `now`.

exports.name: SCHEDULE_AHEAD_SECONDS
exports.summary: How far ahead of `now` boundaries are committed, in seconds: the article's 100 ms.

exports.name: SCHEDULER_POLL_MS
exports.summary: How often to poll the scheduler, in milliseconds: the article's 25 ms.

exports.name: SchedulerAnchor
exports.summary: The audio-time / step pair a running clock is anchored to, for deriving the display position.

exports.name: SchedulerConfig
exports.summary: What the scheduler steps through: the window of steps it loops over and how long a step lasts, read on every call.

exports.name: SchedulerCursor
exports.summary: Where the scheduler is: the next step it will emit and when.

exports.name: StepBoundary
exports.summary: A step to play and the audio time it starts at.

exports.name: BarsBeats
exports.summary: A position in bars, beats and sixteenths, each counted from one.

exports.name: barsBeatsAt
exports.summary: Where `seconds` falls in bars, beats and sixteenths, each counted from one.

exports.name: bpmToMicrosecondsPerQuarterNote
exports.summary: A tempo in BPM as microseconds per quarter note, the unit a MIDI file stores: 120 BPM is 500000.

exports.name: DEFAULT_MICROSECONDS_PER_QUARTER_NOTE
exports.summary: What a file with no Set Tempo event plays at: 120 BPM, 500,000 microseconds a quarter note.

exports.name: DEFAULT_TEMPO
exports.summary: 120 BPM in 4/4.

exports.name: describeBarsBeats
exports.summary: "Bar 3, beat 2", the way a position is read out to a screen reader.

exports.name: microsecondsPerQuarterNoteToBpm
exports.summary: The BPM of a Set Tempo's microseconds per quarter note: 500000 is 120.

exports.name: secondsPerBar
exports.summary: Seconds per bar: a beat times the beats in a bar.

exports.name: secondsPerBeat
exports.summary: Seconds per beat, a beat being one `beatUnit` note: in 6/8, half a quarter.

exports.name: secondsPerQuarter
exports.summary: Seconds per quarter note: BPM counts quarters whatever the signature says.

exports.name: Tempo
exports.summary: Tempo and time signature: how long a quarter note, a beat and a bar last in seconds, and where a position in seconds falls in bars and beats.

exports.name: addWarpMarker
exports.summary: Adds a marker at a time on the clip, pinning what plays there; nothing changes in how it plays until it moves.

exports.name: moveWarpMarker
exports.summary: Moves the marker at `index` to a new time on the clip, stretching the recording on either side of it: it stops short of its neighbours.

exports.name: removeWarpMarker
exports.summary: Takes the marker at `index` away, as long as two are left to make a map.

exports.name: scaleWarp
exports.summary: Plays the whole map `factor` times as long: 2 is half the speed, an octave down; 0.5 twice the speed.

exports.name: unwarpedTime
exports.summary: What time in the source plays at a time on the clip.

exports.name: WarpMarker
exports.summary: A time in the source, pinned to a time on the clip.

exports.name: warpedTime
exports.summary: Where on the clip a time in the source plays.

exports.name: warpMarkers
exports.summary: The markers that make a map: finite ones, in order, each later than the one before in both times.

exports.name: warpRate
exports.summary: How fast the source plays at a time on the clip: 1 as recorded, 2 twice as fast.

exports.name: loadWorklet
exports.summary: Loads the source of an `AudioWorklet` processor into a context, from a blob, so there is no file to serve.

exports.name: LaneSamples
exports.summary: A recording's samples, mixed to one: how many frames it holds, and a reader of the frames from `from` to `to`.

exports.name: LaneSpectra
exports.summary: A recording's spectra: a column every `hop` frames, each bin's level to Nyquist over windows of `size` frames, a byte each, (dB + 150) · 1.6, 0 silence: what `gl-spectrogram` draws a recording it does not hold from.

exports.name: CHUNK_FRAMES
exports.summary: The frames a renderer keeps its samples in, and a streamed recording is read in: 65536.

exports.name: ChunkFeed
exports.summary: What a renderer holds of a recording it streams: the chunks handed over, oldest first, and those being read.

exports.name: ChunkRenderer
exports.summary: What a renderer that streams its samples does with them: `gl-waveform` and `gl-spectrogram` both do.

exports.name: feedChunks
exports.summary: Hands a renderer the chunks of a streamed recording that `ranges` read, in frames: those it lacks are read, each handed over once read, and `ready` draws again.

exports.name: LaneSegment
exports.summary: A stretch of a clip that reads its recording straight on: its two times in the clip, in seconds from its start, and the frames of the recording at them.

exports.name: LaneClip
exports.summary: A clip of a lane to draw: where it lies, how long it is, and how it reads its recording.

exports.name: VisiblePart
exports.summary: A part of a clip the view shows: its part of the canvas in CSS px from the canvas' left, and the frames of the recording it reads there.

exports.name: VisibleClip
exports.summary: A clip the view shows, with its parts and its samples.

exports.name: OVERSCAN
exports.summary: The pixels drawn past each edge of the view, so a scroll shows them at once.

exports.name: groundOf
exports.summary: The nearest background that is not transparent, from `element` up: what a picture's silence lies over.

exports.name: hasWebGL2
exports.summary: Whether this browser can draw with WebGL 2: the lanes that need it say no, and the page draws them another way.

exports.name: releaseContext
exports.summary: Lets go of a lane's own WebGL context once the lane is destroyed: a browser keeps only some sixteen, frees a dropped canvas's only when it collects it, and past that loses the oldest, which may be one a page still draws on.

exports.name: keepContext
exports.summary: A lane starts on a canvas whose context was being let go of: it keeps it.

exports.name: sameSamples
exports.summary: Whether two readings are the same samples: a reader may hand out a new view of the same memory each time, which is not new data to upload.

exports.name: clearLane
exports.summary: Clears the whole canvas of a lane's context.

exports.name: Placed
exports.summary: What `placeLane` gives: where the canvas starts on the lane, in CSS px, where it ends, and the device pixel ratio.

exports.name: placeLane
exports.summary: Sizes the canvas to the stretch of its lane the view shows, and gives that stretch in CSS px from the lane's left with the device pixel ratio, or hides the canvas when none shows: the lane scrolled out of sight to either side, or up or down.

exports.name: joinParts
exports.summary: Parts that follow one another on the canvas and in the recording, joined into one while every junction between them stays within a quarter of a pixel of where the one line reading them all puts it: a warped clip's stretches, a pixel or two wide zoomed out, are drawn as one part, not hundreds, and stay apart zoomed in, where a junction would show.

exports.name: partsInView
exports.summary: The clips of a lane the view shows, each with its parts, before their samples are read: stretches that read as one line joined (`joinParts`).

exports.name: SampleCache
exports.summary: What a lane has read of its recordings, by `source`: a recording is read once, not at every paint, since a reader may copy or mix the whole of it each time it is asked.

exports.name: KeptCache
exports.summary: What a lane has read of its recordings, by key: what it read, or is reading, and the reader it read it with.

exports.name: readKept
exports.summary: What `read` gives for `samples`, from `cache` under `key` when that reader is the one it was read with, else read now and kept: once a promise is settled, the cache holds what it gave, so the next paint has it at once.

exports.name: readOnce
exports.summary: A recording's samples, from the cache when its reader is the one it was read with, else read now and kept.

exports.name: visibleClipsNow
exports.summary: The clips of a lane the view shows, as `visibleClips` gives them, when every recording they read hands its samples at once: what lets a lane draw a zoom in the frame it happens.

exports.name: visibleClips
exports.summary: The clips of a lane the view shows, each with its parts of the canvas and the frames it reads there, and their samples read once a recording.

exports.name: LaneContext
exports.summary: What a lane hands its painter and its listeners.

exports.name: LaneOptions
exports.summary: What a lane is made of.

exports.name: Lane
exports.summary: A lane that is drawing.

exports.name: createLane
exports.summary: Starts a lane on `canvas`, which sits in the lane's box: placed on the stretch the view shows, drawn again when its inputs change, the lane resizes, the view scrolls a good way or the theme changes, and let go of with `destroy`.

exports.name: SpectrogramScale
exports.summary: The frequency axes a spectrogram is spaced on: octaves, mel, equal space per auditory filter, or hertz.

exports.name: SpectrogramBand
exports.summary: The frequencies a spectrogram shows, as shares of its axis from 0 (the floor) to 1 (the Nyquist limit), whatever the axis spaces its rows by: the clips draw this band, the axis labels it.

exports.name: zoomBand
exports.summary: The band `factor` times as wide (under 1 zooms in), the share `at` of it (0 at its foot) staying where it is.

exports.name: panBand
exports.summary: The band moved by `share` of its own width, up or down, kept inside the axis.

exports.name: loadScales
exports.summary: The axes the rows are spaced on, for labels that match them: `scales[name].at(f, lo, hi)` is where `f` hertz sits between `lo` and `hi`, 0 to 1.

exports.name: SpectrogramHit
exports.summary: What the pointer is over on a spectrogram: the cell's frequencies and level, the floor of the levels drawn, and where the pointer is.

exports.name: SpectrogramInputs
exports.summary: What a spectrogram lane draws.

exports.name: SpectrogramHooks
exports.summary: What a spectrogram lane tells its host.

exports.name: createSpectrogramLane
exports.summary: Draws the spectrograms of a lane's clips on `canvas`, which sits in the lane's box, each clip in its own part of it: their frequencies over the stretch of the lane the view shows, computed on the GPU by `gl-spectrogram` at every zoom, in the text colour over the ground under it.

exports.name: readHertz
exports.summary: A frequency the pointer reads, as the axis writes it: three significant digits, five characters at most (12.3k, 523, 52.3).

exports.name: hertzLabel
exports.summary: A frequency as the axis writes it, no unit: 500, 1.25k, 20k.

exports.name: SpectrogramAxisLayout
exports.summary: What `spectrogramAxis` lays out: a frequency's place, the labels with their ticks, the ticks between, and where the pointer is.

exports.name: spectrogramAxis
exports.summary: Lays out a spectrogram's frequency axis for a lane `height` px tall, as audio.js draws it: labels roundest first (20k, 2k, 200, then between as room allows), each with its tick at the row its frequency sits on by the axis the picture is spaced on, and shorter ticks between, the band in view respected.

exports.name: hasWebGL2
exports.summary: Whether this browser can draw with WebGL 2: the lanes that need it say no, and the page draws them another way.

exports.name: Lane

exports.summary: A clip of a lane to draw: where it lies, how long it is, and how it reads its recording.

exports.name: LaneSamples
exports.summary: A recording's samples, mixed to one: how many frames it holds, and a reader of the frames from `from` to `to`.

exports.name: LaneSpectra
exports.summary: A recording's spectra: a column every `hop` frames, each bin's level to Nyquist over windows of `size` frames, a byte each, (dB + 150) · 1.6, 0 silence: what `gl-spectrogram` draws a recording it does not hold from.

exports.name: WaveformBands
exports.summary: The three signals a sound is split into to colour it by its frequencies: what it has low, between and high.

exports.name: WaveformClip
exports.summary: A clip of the lane, with what its waveform needs besides what every lane clip has.

exports.name: WaveformLook
exports.summary: How the lane draws a waveform: as one, or as the three bands of the sound one over the other, the lows warm and the highs cool.

exports.name: WaveformLayout
exports.summary: How a recording with several channels is laid out: `mix` draws them as one waveform; `split` draws each channel in a row of its own, as a DAW does on a tall track; `auto` splits when each row would be at least `SPLIT_ROW_PX` tall, and mixes below that, as a short track shows one lane.

exports.name: SPLIT_ROW_PX
exports.summary: The least height of a channel's row, in CSS px, for `auto` to split.

exports.name: WaveformInputs
exports.summary: What a waveform lane draws.

exports.name: WaveformLaneOptions
exports.summary: How a waveform lane draws.

exports.name: LEAF_FRAMES
exports.summary: The frames a leaf of `waveformLeaves` sums up.

exports.name: waveformLeaves
exports.summary: The leaves of `samples`, from its first frame: `[min, max, Σx², count]` of each 256 frames, the last leaf of what is left, NaN left out (a leaf of nothing else is `[Infinity, -Infinity, 0, 0]`).

exports.name: leavesPeak
exports.summary: The loudest sample the leaves sum up, 0 to 1 for a recording at full scale at most: what a streamed clip's `peak` is.

exports.name: WaveformRow
exports.summary: What a clip draws in one row of the lane: a layer of its recording, its samples, the loudest of them, and the row's place and height.

exports.name: splitsChannels
exports.summary: Whether a clip draws each channel in a row of its own at this layout, look and height.

exports.name: waveformRows
exports.summary: The rows a clip draws in a lane `height` px tall, with the samples of each: a channel apiece (`channels`, read), its recording whole, or its three bands.

exports.name: createWaveformLane
exports.summary: Draws the waveforms of a lane's clips on `canvas`, which sits in the lane's box, each clip in its own parts of it, on the GPU by `gl-waveform`: every pixel column shows the exact lowest and highest of its samples with the RMS inside, and zoomed in a line through the samples, however long the recording.

exports.summary: Whether this browser can draw with WebGL 2: the lanes that need it say no, and the page draws them another way.
